answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable stake that cannot be faked in bulk — like requiring every agent to lock a small bond before it may transact. One attacker can spin up a thousand fake accounts, but cannot fund a thousand bonds without real cost. Think of it as a quartz filter at the inlet of the network: only agents that pass the stake check flow through, while the fable of free, infinite identities collapses once each new identity carries a price.
